DDOS is a Distributed Denial of service attack. Meaning that many computers (usually a botnet) will send fake requests to the website, but never actually complete it. For example, somebody knocking at your front door and hiding, you go back inside, nobody there! Then another knock, and another, but every time you check there's nobody there.

So basically they are sending in millions of these per second / minute to the server to overload it, making real requests longer to get to since you are taking so much time answering to nothing.

Some servers will just slow down to a crawl, some will crash because they can't handle it anymore.

This is why many sites these days use a anti DDOS service which filters out bad requests, kind of like putting a body guard at the front to make sure you are who you say you are and not just some asshole who wants to knock and run.

I would tell you to avoid the Remastered version, but I guess it's too late now?

Primarily, the Homeworld: Remastered is simply Homeworld ported to Homeworld 2 engine. Unfortunately, Homeworld 2 was a quite different game so many things from original Homeworld are either gone or don't work as they should.

For example, in Homeworld every ship was its own entity, while Homeworld 2 introduced squadrons that act as a single unit. One Homeworld was ported, this difference in behavior broke formations in the game. They only work until combat, once a fight starts every ship does whatever the hell it wants, usually with horrible results(like Heavy Corvettes trying to orbit the target, therefore being only able to use half their guns).

In Homeworld, every projectile was an physically simulated entity, so i.e. if it didn't hit the target it could hit something behind the target if it was there. In HW2, damage is down to RNG and in-space projectiles are just a graphics effect. A minor change, but a step backwards nevertheless.

Resource model is the HW2 one, not the HW one.

Ship "progression" is from HW2, which makes strike craft basically obsolete once you get to the big guns.

There are numerous bugs, oversights and inconsistencies in the game in general(audio, script, missions).

And so on.

The original Homeworld works just fine on modern PCs/resolutions with the minimum amount of tweaking so there's really no reason to bother with the Remastered version.
